AC: Can authenticate to Ameriprise; can read account balances; can read positions; can read transaction history; skill/tool documented for agent use

Body.raw:
Create a skill or tool for programmatic access to Ameriprise brokerage/investment
accounts for agent use: positions, balances, and transaction history. Order
placement is OUT of the current AC (see D1).

## Research findings (2026-08 grooming pass)

**No public API.** Ameriprise publishes no developer API. Third-party access is
via aggregators only; Plaid does list "Ameriprise Financial - My Financial
Accounts", but self-hosting a Plaid integration needs a Plaid account with
production access and is read-only aggregation anyway. Treat Plaid as a last
resort, not a shortcut.

**A sanctioned machine path exists: OFX Direct Connect.** Ameriprise's own
Quicken FAQ (ameriprise.com/customer-service/quicken-faqs) documents Direct
Connect for brokerage accounts, no fee, up to 90 days of activity, plus Web
Connect (manual QFX download from the secure site). Direct Connect requires a
ONE-TIME identity verification: the user enters their online User ID and password
on an Ameriprise verification page to enable the download method. This is the
cheapest, most durable and most defensible path, and OFX returns exactly what the
AC asks for: INVSTMTRS transactions, INCPOS positions, INVBAL balances.

- `ofxtools` (csingley) ships the FI profile:
  url `https://www25.ameriprise.com/AMPFWeb/ofxdl/us/download?request_type=nl_desktopdownload`,
  version 211, org `AMPF`, fid `3102` (alt `13573`), brokerid `ameriprise.com`.
  A separate entry covers the Ameriprise MasterCard at `ofx.ameriprise.com`
  (org `Ameriprise MasterCard`, fid `12910`).
- `ofxtools` is pure stdlib, Python 3.10+, deliberately complete on the OFX
  investment message set, and its `ofxget` CLI already stores passwords in the
  system keyring. It is the obvious dependency.
- **RISK, unproven:** whether that endpoint still answers a third-party client.
  form8949.com states Ameriprise "hosts an OFX server. However, they restrict
  access to the server such that we cannot retrieve your data on your behalf."
  Historical Moneydance/GnuCash reports show OFX error 2000 and
  `PROFMSGSRQV1`-unsupported failures. Quicken community threads show Ameriprise
  Direct Connect working for Quicken clients (with periodic breakage), so the
  server is live for *some* clients. Settle this by spike before building.
- Direct Connect MFA is `CLIENTUID`-based (Intuit's OFX MFA scheme), not an OTP
  prompt: some institutions bind a UUID per client install, and some accept only
  a UUID minted by real Quicken. `ofxtools` defaults `appid=QWIN`,
  `appver=2700`, i.e. the working path probably requires identifying as Quicken
  (see L2).

**Web portal 2FA is mandatory and unavoidable on the browser path.** Ameriprise
requires 2-Step Verification for all secure-site access. Second factors: the
Ameriprise Financial app push notification, a THIRD-PARTY AUTHENTICATOR APP
(TOTP), or SMS/automated voice 6-digit OTP; passkeys/FIDO2 security keys are
offered as a passwordless first factor. Only the third-party authenticator
automates cleanly: enroll a TOTP secret once, keep it in the same secret store as
the password, compute codes locally with `pyotp`. App push, SMS and voice all
need a human or an SMS bridge. Repeated wrong codes SUSPEND online access, so
retry logic must be conservative (see L3).

**Mobile app reverse engineering: deprioritized.** A 2026 financial app should be
assumed to use certificate pinning plus platform attestation (Play Integrity /
App Attest). Bypass means Frida/objection instrumentation on a rooted device or a
patched APK: high effort, brittle against app updates, and a materially worse
ToS/CFAA posture than the sanctioned OFX path. Revisit only if OFX and the portal
both fail.

**Existing OSS: nothing Ameriprise-specific.** Prior art worth modelling the
layout on: `eebette/bank_scrapers` (per-institution Playwright drivers; notably
already has a Fidelity NetBenefits driver, relevant to sibling todo `96314836`),
`thrashr888/till` (CLI plus per-source Playwright plugins, OS keychain
credentials, local SQLite), `wnstnb/foliome` (Playwright with config-driven
readers).

## Legal / ToS constraints (acknowledge, do not assume away)

- **L1.** Ameriprise Terms of Use (ameriprise.com/legal/website-rules) prohibit
  "unauthorized use of Ameriprise's Website and systems, including ...
  unauthorized entry into Ameriprise's systems, misuse of passwords" and reserve
  termination of access at sole discretion, without notice. Reading one's OWN
  accounts with one's OWN credentials is the benign case, but automated access is
  nowhere affirmatively blessed.
- **L2.** The OFX path's practical need to present `appid=QWIN` is client
  impersonation. Every OSS OFX client does it (GnuCash/AqBanking, Moneydance,
  ofxtools defaults) and Ameriprise charges no fee for Direct Connect, but it is a
  deliberate risk the user must accept (D5).
- **L3.** The failure mode is account access SUSPENSION, not merely an error:
  repeated bad one-time codes or denied push prompts lock online access. Hard
  guardrails: no credential guessing, at most one OTP attempt per login, low
  request frequency, and no unattended retry loop on auth failure.
- **L4.** Writes raise the stakes categorically - a bug moves money or places an
  order. Excluded from the AC by default (D1).

## Open decisions - BLOCKING, user input needed (do not guess)

- **D1. Read-only or read-write?** The AC as written is read-only
  (balances/positions/transactions); the original body floated "potentially
  placing orders". Recommendation: read-only for v1, a separate todo for any
  trading capability. CONFIRM.
- **D2. Which account types are in scope?** Brokerage / SPS Advantage only, or
  also the Ameriprise MasterCard (separate OFX endpoint and fid), RiverSource
  annuities (riversource.com, separate portal), managed/wrap accounts? Each extra
  type adds an endpoint or a whole portal.
- **D3. Credential and TOTP-secret storage:** system keyring (`ofxget` already
  supports it), `pass`/GPG, 1Password CLI (`op read`), or an env/secret file?
  No precedent exists in this repo - nothing here stores third-party credentials
  today, so this sets one.
- **D4. 2FA contract when a code IS required:** fully unattended via a stored
  TOTP secret (requires the user to enroll a third-party authenticator app and
  hand the tool the shared secret), or interactive prompt / `--otp` flag with a
  human in the loop, or both with unattended as opt-in?
- **D5. Risk acceptance:** is Quicken emulation (`appid=QWIN`) for Direct Connect
  acceptable, and is Playwright automation of the user's own secure-site login
  acceptable? If neither is, the only remaining paths are parsing manually
  exported Web Connect QFX / tax CSV files, or Plaid.
- **D6. Layout and naming** (currently provisional in `Scope.path_from_root`): a
  new top-level `brokerage/` project (per-institution drivers, shared normalizer,
  its own `.venv/` per AGENTS.md) plus a thin `skills/brokerage-access/SKILL.md`,
  shared with the Fidelity 401k todo? Or an Ameriprise-only project and skill?
- **D7. Persistence:** print JSON per invocation, or also persist a local SQLite
  history? Direct Connect exposes only a 90-day window, so history not captured
  is history lost.

## Decomposition note

All work stays as parent-local WorkItems; no subtodos. The phases are
sequentially gated - the OFX spike decides whether the browser driver is written
at all - and each item is a single-subsystem commit with no independent
branch-bound artifact to farm out. Sibling todo `96314836` (Fidelity 401k
NetBenefits) is the natural consumer of whatever is extracted as shared
(credential store, TOTP handling, normalized schema, CLI shell); cross-link, do
not nest.

LongSummary.raw:
Programmatic read access to the owner's own Ameriprise Financial brokerage and
investment accounts - balances, positions, and transaction history - exposed to
agents as a CLI plus a SKILL.md. Ameriprise publishes no developer API, so
grooming research settled on OFX Direct Connect as the primary path: Ameriprise's
own Quicken FAQ documents fee-free Direct Connect for brokerage accounts with a
90-day activity window, and the ofxtools Python library already ships the
connection profile (url www25.ameriprise.com/AMPFWeb/ofxdl, org AMPF, fid 3102 or
13573, brokerid ameriprise.com, OFX version 211) along with full investment
message set support for INVSTMTRQ transactions, INCPOS positions and INVBAL
balances.

Two things are unproven and gate the build. First, whether that OFX endpoint
still answers a third-party client at all: form8949.com reports that Ameriprise
restricts server access, and GnuCash and Moneydance users have hit OFX error 2000
and PROFMSGSRQV1-unsupported failures, while Quicken users do get working
downloads. Second, whether the server demands an Intuit-style CLIENTUID and an
appid=QWIN Quicken identity. Direct Connect additionally requires a one-time
identity verification the user performs by hand on the Ameriprise secure site.
The first WorkItem is therefore a probe, not an implementation. Ranked alternates
are browser automation of the secure site with Playwright (modelled on
eebette/bank_scrapers and thrashr888/till), then parsing manually exported Web
Connect QFX or tax CSV files, then Plaid. Mobile app reverse engineering is
deliberately excluded: certificate pinning plus platform attestation make it
brittle, and its terms-of-service posture is far worse than the sanctioned path.

Ameriprise requires 2-Step Verification on every secure-site login. The only
cleanly automatable factor is a third-party authenticator app, meaning a stored
TOTP secret evaluated locally with pyotp; app push notifications, SMS and voice
codes all need a human in the loop. Repeated bad codes suspend online access, so
auth retry must be conservative rather than persistent, and Ameriprise's Terms of
Use nowhere bless automated access even to one's own accounts.

Order placement is out of scope - the acceptance criteria are read-only. Grooming
deliberately left seven decisions with the user instead of guessing them:
read-only versus read-write, which account types count (brokerage and SPS
Advantage versus the separately-hosted Ameriprise MasterCard, RiverSource
annuities, and managed accounts), where the password and TOTP secret live
(system keyring, pass, or 1Password) given this repo stores no third-party
credentials today, whether 2FA runs unattended or prompts, whether Quicken
emulation and browser automation of one's own login are acceptable risks, the
project layout, and whether transaction history is persisted locally since Direct
Connect only exposes 90 days.

Sibling todo 96314836 wants the same capability for a Fidelity 401k through
NetBenefits. The credential store, TOTP handling, normalized
account/position/transaction schema and CLI shell are the intended shared pieces,
which is why a `brokerage/` project holding per-institution drivers is the
provisional layout rather than an Ameriprise-only tool.

[MIDCAP] Spike A - probe the Ameriprise OFX endpoint. ofxget scan plus a profile request against www25.ameriprise.com/AMPFWeb/ofxdl (org AMPF, fid 3102 and 13573, version 211, brokerid ameriprise.com), and the ofx.ameriprise.com MasterCard entry if D2 includes it. Record per attempt: HTTP status, OFX status code, whether PROFMSGSRQV1 answers, whether CLIENTUID is demanded, whether appid=QWIN is required. Commit findings as a notes file. Escalate to HICAP if failures are ambiguous rather than flat refusals.

[MIDCAP] Spike A2 (user in the loop, expect a userneeded pause) - have the user complete Ameriprise's one-time Quicken Direct Connect identity verification on the secure site, then re-run signon plus one INVSTMTRQ against a real acctid. Outcome is the go/no-go on OFX vs the browser fallback; record the verdict in the notes file.

[MIDCAP] Fixtures - capture a redacted sample of whatever the winning path returns (an INVSTMTRS response, or a Web Connect QFX / tax CSV exported by hand from the secure site) under a fixtures dir, with account numbers, names and dollar amounts scrubbed. Fast tests must never need live credentials.

[HICAP] Exemplar - one normalizer module mapping OFX INVSTMTRS, INVPOSLIST and INVBAL into dataclasses (Account, Balance, Position, Transaction) with stable field names and Decimal money, plus a golden-file test over the redacted fixture. Land the pattern once here; roll out further transaction subtypes as separate MIDCAP items.

[MIDCAP] Secret access seam per D3 - one resolver that fetches user id, password and (if D4 requires) the TOTP secret from the chosen store, with no plaintext credential ever written to the repo, the todo store, or a log. Include a test using a fake provider.

[MIDCAP] Auth flow per D4 - TOTP code generation (pyotp) for unattended runs plus an interactive/--otp path for a human, and persisted CLIENTUID and session reuse so a successful login is not re-earned every invocation. Hard rule from L3: at most one OTP attempt per login, and no retry loop on auth failure (repeated bad codes suspend online access).

[MIDCAP] CONDITIONAL, only if Spike A/A2 fail - Playwright secure-site driver that logs in, clears 2-Step Verification, and pulls balances, positions and transactions, preferring the site's own export/download over DOM scraping, feeding the same normalizer. Model the layout on eebette/bank_scrapers and thrashr888/till.

[MIDCAP] CLI surface - subcommands accounts, balances, positions, transactions with --json output over the normalizer. Project .venv created via ./create_pipenv.sh per AGENTS.md; Makefile test target runs fixtures-only fast tests, all-tests covers the live network/credential path.

[LOCAP] Run and report - make test in the project, plus a grep-level check that no fixture, log or committed file carries a real account number, password or TOTP secret. Escalate the fix, not the re-run, on red.

[MIDCAP] Skill doc per D6 - write SKILL.md covering agent-facing invocation, the one-time setup preconditions (Direct Connect identity verification, authenticator-app enrollment, secret store population), the L1-L4 ToS and lockout guardrails, and each known failure mode with what it means.

[MIDCAP] Extract the institution-independent pieces (secret resolver, TOTP, normalized schema, CLI shell) behind a stable seam and write down the reuse contract for the Fidelity 401k todo 96314836; add an INFO cross-link, not a tracked subtodo.
